newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Wessex sees no supply disruptions.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Wessex sees no supply disruptions.

text.p: British water utility Wessex Water Plc does not expect to have any problems with supplies either this year or next year, chairman Nicholas Hood told Reuters.
"We've got no problems with interruptions to supply...we've never had any for 25 years, we won't have any this year or next year," Hood said in a telephone interview.
He said this meant leakage was not such an issue for Wessex as it was for others. The company was on course to cut current leakage levels of 23 percent to 15 percent by 2005.
The new Labour government has said it will introduce mandatory leakage targets as part of a 10-point plan to cope with the current drought, Britain's worst for 200 years.
Hood said he was sure the government would agree to a sensible target.
"I see no reason why it should be any lower or higher than the one which we have set for ourselves," he said.
Wessex saw annual pretax profits rise eight percent to 145 million stg and paid out a dividend of 18 pence per share, up from 15.2 pence.

Hood said the dividend increase reflected the performance of the non-core business and at the core business -- particularly in cutting costs, as well as a reduction in the number of shares in issue after a buyback earlier this year.

The company's non-core UK Waste business had "adjusted to the imposition of the landfill tax very well," benefiting from pressure on companies to find alternative forms of waste disposal such as recycling, he said.
Hood was optimistic about all areas of the business.
But he added the substantial cost cuts seen for the fifth successive year could not go on forever.
Although savings would begin to level off, there were more to come.
